title: Organizations whose files drew a no more than once
question: Is there any organization whose contracts, grants or leases were voted against at more than one final vote?
finding: 9 organizations other than public bodies are named in two or more money files that drew a no at the final vote: San Francisco Pretrial Diversion Project, Inc. (4 of its 5 files, on 4 days); Friends of the San Francisco Public Library (4 of its 14 files, on 3 days); New Cingular Wireless PCS, LLC (3 of its 6 files, on 3 days); Oryx Development I, LLC (2 of its 2 files, on 2 days); Intersection Media, LLC (2 of its 2 files, on 2 days); Bank of America, N.A. (2 of its 3 files, on 1 day). In every case the files passed. 2 of the 9 owe at least one of those noes to a same-day list on which one member voted against every file. Set against 1,368 organizations named in files with a final vote, repeat dissent is rare.
how: Each money file with a final vote is credited to the organizations its title names (the party as read from the title; private persons are left out). An organization is listed when two or more of its files drew at least one no. “Files with a final vote” is every file naming it, so the share shows how unusual a no was for that organization. Public bodies, such as a State department whose grant the City accepts, are marked and listed last.
limits: A divided vote is not a sign about the organization, and none is attached to any organization on this site. The same members often vote no on the same programme year after year for reasons of policy: the vote pages give no reasons. Names are matched as the titles print them, so an organization whose name is spelled two ways is split, and an organization named only in an unusual phrase is missed. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
